title: STUDY TOPIC Loving righteousness Part 1
devotional:
One of the best known parts of the bible is what people call the ‘Sermon on the Mount’ which is recorded in Matthew 5-7. Much has been written and said about the Sermon on the Mount. I think the best way to understand it is to see it as Jesus giving us an extended, redefined understanding of righteousness. In the Sermon, Jesus describes for us, what true righteousness is like.

When we hear the word ‘righteousness’ which is the word Matthew uses for holiness we don’t often get very excited. The word ‘righteousness’ is not famous for being a ‘buzz’ word, it’s not considered cool. We are not the kind of people to get thrilled or animated about living a righteous life. Some of us have been brought up to think that living a righteous life, is a call to joyless boredom and a serious demeanour, which is so far removed for the bibles understanding of righteousness.

The word for righteousness is from the Greek word dikaiosyne which in the broad sense describes a person who is as he ought to be, i.e. discovering his/her full potential. It also carries the idea of justice, integrity, virtue, purity of life, rightness, correctness of thinking, feeling and acting. We need to think of righteousness as something that is extremely positive and desirable. It could be described as a wholesome mature character.

We are going to look at how Jesus redefined righteousness and painted it in bright attractive colours.

Jesus’ ‘new take’ on righteousness.

Righteousness requires an internal passion.

We must approach to issue of righteousness with passionate hearts. Look and how Jesus describes how we should engage with righteousness: -

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” Matt 5:6.

“But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.” Matt 6:33.

We need to develop an energetic and enthusiastic relationship with righteousness, we need to passionately love and enjoy it. We need motivating appetites for righteous living. We need to have a positive emotional relationship with righteousness. Negative emotions such as guilt or shame cannot lead to a righteous life.

Righteousness is satisfying.

In hungering for righteousness we are making a very strong statement, we are refusing to accept or settle for the mediocre or the boring. We are acknowledging that we have the potential to live full and satisfying lives. We are expressing a legitimate need of our hearts. We have been made in such a way that righteous living is extremely satisfying and enhancing. Jesus said “Blessed are they that hunger and thirst for righteousness for they shall be filled.’’ The word filled ‘chortazo’ and it means to eat until one is full.

Righteous living will mean that we will guard our hearts and continually monitor their condition. If you read Matthew chapter 5 carefully, you will notice that Jesus mentions, murder, adultery, divorce and oaths. The Pharisees of Jesus’ day prided themselves in keeping the law, now what they understood by keeping the law was that they never did the physical act. They had never physically murdered someone, or physically slept with another man’s wife. The point that Jesus makes in this passage is, if we have anger or lust in our hearts then we are as guilty as the actual murderer or adulterer.

We are inclined to categorise sin, we think of wee sins, and big sins. That is like categorising cyanide. Is a little cyanide only a little harmful, or is it just as dangerous as a lot of cyanide? Jesus was very clear, he said “Unless your righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.’’ The Pharisees kept the law exactly and meticulously, however, in their hearts they were full of anger, lust and greed.

Righteous living is not about appearance, or about ticking boxes, or about fulfilling the expectations of others, rather it is about the condition of our hearts and what we carry in them.
prayer: Father thank you we have been designed to love and enjoy righteousness.
